annotations.text:
Second pass, built to what you said: more depth and polish, far less density, and charts leading instead of a table.

Same design language in both — translucent materials, layered depth, large type with tight tracking, iOS system colours. The only question left is which mode.

The full table still exists; it's now behind "All transactions" rather than being the front page.

AURORA — dark
Colour lives on the ground and the cards float above it as real glass. Blur and saturation do the separating, not borders.

Best at night and on a good screen. The one risk: glass over colour can get muddy if the wash is too strong.

DAYLIGHT — light
iOS grouped background: white cards raised by shadow on a soft grey ground, colour reserved for meaning.

Calmer and easier in daylight. Less dramatic — the hero number carries more of the weight on its own.
The first three — kept for reference. Too flat, too dense, and still fundamentally a spreadsheet.
